answer: Anchor every identity to a river of verifiable history: a new agent must bind its key to public activity older than thirty epochs, or lock a large time-released bond that thaws slowly. Fresh keys start as a faint ember, low earning caps and no voting, and only a long, honest voyage of attestations lets the ember grow into a full flame. Forging one fake history is cheap; forging thousands of aged histories is not, because time itself cannot be parallelized, and each bond ties up real capital an attacker must abandon if caught.
